newsitem.title: USA: Ag dept probes strawberry packer.
newsitem.headline: Ag dept probes strawberry packer.

text.p: The Agriculture Department said Wednesday the supplier of frozen strawberries that made at least 150 schoolchildren ill is being investigated for possible criminal violations.

Mary Ann Keeffe, an acting undersecretary of the USDA, told reporters that the San Diego firm of Andrew & Williamson, a processor and packer of foods, could face criminal penalties if it is determined that the strawberries were imported from Mexico.
The firm's parent company, Epitope Inc. said earlier that it would recall 13 lots of strawberries that were shipped in early December 1996.

A joint press statement issued by the federal agencies involved said the berries associated with the illness were imported from Mexico. At a news briefing, however, Agriculture Department officials said that the agency was investigating the company's records, and had not yet pinpointed the origin of the strawberries.

The Food and Drug Administration, which has jurisdiction over food processing plants, said they were trying to track down where the remaining berries from the contaminated lots were distributed. "Not all these berries went to the school lunch program," said Michael Friedman, deputy commissioner of the FDA.

The Agriculture Department buys only U.S.-grown commodities for the national school lunch program, and requires companies to certify that their products are domestic. If the company sold Mexican-grown berries to the Agriculture Department, company officials could face criminal penalties of up to five years in prison and fines, officials said.
